solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ruler of Germany given notice by English

indicators.note: being given something means having it attached, so the country's symbol is followed by what comes next

blocks.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
standard abbreviation for English
to spot something is to notice it

explanation.surface: A German leader has been served notice by the English, as in some diplomatic snub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by English' places E beside the notice, so the order runs D, E, then SPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is an absolute ruler, typically a tyrannical one.

clue.text: Died subduing fanatical giant slayer

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing subduing another sits on top of it, so this piece is written above

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for died
an avid fan is a fanatical one

explanation.surface: Someone died while overpowering a crazed enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, the young David killed the giant Goliath with a sling.

clue.text: Strange creature crossing river in ancient city

indicators.note: an animal crossing something stretches over it, so its letters straddle what follows
the waterway sitting in the city is placed right at its end, joining the two pieces

blocks.note: a seal is a sea creature
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city, a crossword regular
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An odd animal wades across a river in an old Mesopotamian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange creature' reads as one phrase, but 'Strange' alone is the definition and the creature is just the outer shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Surreal describes something bizarre and dreamlike, a close synonym of strange.

clue.text: Grow a vine at sea? That's impressive!

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and lost, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Cultivating grapes on a ship would indeed be a remarkable achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' pretends to be a location for the vineyard; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overawing fills people with awe, which is to say it is deeply impressive.

clue.text: Times editor on vacation doesn't need one?

definitions.text: Times editor on vacation doesn't need one?

indicators.note: a word on vacation has been vacated, emptied of everything but its outer letters

blocks.note: eras are periods of time
the word emptied of its inside letters

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor on holiday makes no corrections, so has no use for a rubbing-out tool.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: an editor who is away fixes no mistakes. 'Times' looks like the newspaper but supplies the periods.
explanation.definitionFit: An eraser rubs out mistakes, a tool an editor uses only while actually at work.

clue.text: Ne'er-do-well lexicographer detailed features typical of upper classes

indicators.note: de-tailed means having the tail removed, so the name loses its final letter
a thing that features something includes it within itself

blocks.note: Peter Mark Roget compiled the famous Thesaurus
U is the old label for upper-class usage, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: A disreputable dictionary-maker gives a meticulous account of the traits of the posh.
explanation.walkthrough: ROGET loses its T to become ROGE, and U goes inside it. 'Detailed' poses as 'thorough' but means tail cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest or unprincipled person, the same as a good-for-nothing ne'er-do-well.

clue.text: Deplorable tussle involving hotel detectives

indicators.note: something deplorable is in a wretched state, so these letters are knocked out of shape
to involve something is to take it in, so one letter sits inside the rest

blocks.note: taken as written
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A disgraceful scuffle in a hotel draws in the police investigators.
explanation.walkthrough: TUSSLE is rearranged into SLEUTS, and H goes in before the last S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleuths is an informal word for detectives, from the idea of following a trail.

clue.text: Normally itinerary includes popular locality's periphery

indicators.note: the journey plan includes the next word, holding it inside
the periphery of a word is its edge, so only its outermost letters count

blocks.note: a route is a planned itinerary
something in is fashionable or popular
first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Usually a travel plan takes in the edges of a well-liked area.
explanation.definitionFit: Routinely means as a matter of routine, which is to say normally or usually.

clue.text: Invigilate first of exams on love poetry

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter only
in an across clue, one piece on another comes after it

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
verse is poetry
opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An instruction to supervise an exam whose topic is romantic poems.
explanation.definitionFit: To invigilate is to supervise candidates during an exam, a specific kind of overseeing.

clue.text: Tormented genius defends old geological classification

indicators.note: a tormented thing is twisted and wracked, so these letters are mixed up
to defend something is to surround and protect it

blocks.note: taken as written
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A troubled brilliant scientist stands up for an outdated way of sorting rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old' looks like it describes the classification, but it only supplies a single letter to be enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Igneous is one of the three main categories of rock, formed from cooled magma.

clue.text: Desperate maniac's last on Conservative list

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter alone
in a down clue one piece written on top of another comes first

blocks.note: a dire situation is a desperate one
final letter of the word
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A frantic madman ends up on a Conservative party roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A directory is an organised list of names, addresses or numbers.

clue.text: A doctor essentially sent some cocaine as stimulant

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letters are kept

blocks.note: taken as written
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
middle two letters of the word
a, as in 'a few', means some
a line is a single dose of cocaine laid out for snorting

explanation.surface: A doctor prescribed a little cocaine to perk someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrenaline is a hormone that acts as a natural stimulant, raising heart rate and alertness.

clue.text: Matching receptacle filled with whiskey

indicators.note: a receptacle filled with something holds it inside

blocks.note: a tin is a container
W is Whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A pair of identical flasks, each topped up with whiskey.
explanation.definitionFit: Twin, as an adjective, describes one of an identical pair, so matching.

clue.text: Small store reportedly supplies populous city

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than read, so the word is taken by its spoken form

blocks.note: a deli is a small shop selling cooked meats and cheeses

explanation.surface: A corner shop, it is said, keeps a whole metropolis fed.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi, India's capital territory, is one of the most populous cities in the world.

clue.text: Acting hesitantly, princess leads the band

indicators.note: one who leads goes in front, so this piece starts the word

blocks.note: Di was the familiar name of Diana, Princess of Wales
taken as written
a ring is a band, as on a finger

explanation.surface: A nervous royal steps out in front of the musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests musicians but means a circular band.
explanation.definitionFit: Dithering is being indecisive, unable to make up one's mind, which is acting hesitantly.

clue.text: In finale, female stalking Steerpike is caught

indicators.note: someone stalking another follows behind, so that piece comes second
the following pair is placed in the word for an ending

blocks.note: a finale is the end
the setter, Steerpike, refers to themself as me
she is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: In the closing scene, a woman tails the setter, who is finally trapped.
explanation.walkthrough: When setters name themselves in a clue, read it as the first-person pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmeshed means tangled in a net, so caught or trapped.

clue.text: Icy mists obscured medium's spiritual practices

indicators.note: something obscured is blurred out of recognition, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for medium, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A clairvoyant's séance is shrouded in cold fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medium' pretends to be the spiritualist but gives just M.
explanation.definitionFit: Mysticism is the pursuit of union with the divine through contemplation and spiritual devotion.

clue.text: Honest view about art retrospective

indicators.note: a retrospective looks back, so the word is read from end to start
one thing about another goes around it

blocks.note: a sight is a view
taken as written

explanation.surface: A frank critic's opinion of a gallery show looking back over an artist's career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospective' looks like an exhibition but tells you to reverse ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight, as in a straight answer, means honest and direct.

clue.text: Car trip abandoned by university examiner

indicators.note: the trip has been abandoned by the next letter, which leaves it

blocks.note: Audi is a German car make
a tour is a trip
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A student's road trip is called off, and an inspector arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor examines financial accounts officially, checking them for accuracy.

clue.text: Tale of lust or yearning

indicators.note: the letters are drawn out of, made up of part of, the words that follow

blocks.note: found across 'luST OR Yearning'

explanation.surface: A romance novel about desire and longing.
explanation.definitionFit: A story is a tale, a narrative of events.

clue.text: Exposed ford in middle of broad Colorado river

indicators.note: something exposed has its covering stripped off, so the outer letters go
the middle of a word is its central letter

blocks.note: the word without its outer letters
taken as written
central letter of the five
CO is the US postal abbreviation for Colorado

explanation.surface: A river crossing laid bare mid-stream in a wide Colorado waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colorado river' looks like a single phrase, but Colorado only gives CO and river is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orinoco is one of South America's great rivers, flowing through Venezuela.

clue.text: Commander in Chief periodically meeting retired US prosecutor

indicators.note: doing something periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken
retired means drawn back, so the abbreviation runs backwards
meeting means joining up with, so the two pieces sit side by side

blocks.note: second and fourth letters of the word
a DA is a District Attorney, an American public prosecutor

explanation.surface: The president, from time to time, meets an American attorney who has stepped down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commander in Chief' reads as one title, but the definition is just 'Commander' and 'in' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A head is a leader or person in charge, so a commander.

clue.text: Verbal form of protest initially disrupted epic trial

indicators.note: initially points to a word's opening letter alone
something disrupted is thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: opening letter of the word
nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A demonstration's first outburst throws a mammoth court case into chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A participle is a form of a verb, like 'running' or 'run', used as an adjective or in compound tenses.

clue.text: Summits held in Alaska epitomised backtracking

indicators.note: the letters are held inside the words that follow
backtracking means going back the way you came, so the letters run right to left

blocks.note: found across 'alaSKA EPitomised'

explanation.surface: Political conferences in Alaska summed up a policy of retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summits' tempts as political meetings; here it means mountain tops.
explanation.definitionFit: Peaks are the tops of mountains, which are their summits.

clue.text: Hang conclusions of liberal inquiry on church!

indicators.note: the conclusions of words are their final letters

blocks.note: last letter of each of the three words
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: An outraged call to string up the results of a liberal investigation into the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' looks like a link joining inquiry to church, but its last letter N is needed too.
explanation.definitionFit: To lynch is to hang someone without trial, by mob action.

clue.text: Victory ceremony one brought to the fore online

indicators.note: the numeral is taken out of its place and moved up to the front

blocks.note: V for victory, as in the V sign
a ritual is a ceremony
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A winners' presentation where one competitor is called up to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: The I in RITUAL moves to its front, giving IRTUAL after V.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtual describes things existing in computer form rather than physically, as in being online.

clue.text: Denies detective's working outside Welsh quarter

indicators.note: the word for working goes outside the next letter, enclosing it

blocks.note: a DI is a Detective Inspector, with the 's kept
a machine that is on is working
W is the abbreviation for Welsh
south is one of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: A police officer rejects charges about operating outside part of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown someone is to refuse to acknowledge them as one's own, so deny or repudiate.

clue.text: Husband concluding fish is tasteless

indicators.note: something concluding a phrase comes at its end, so this letter goes last

blocks.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband's verdict on a dish of fish: bland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tasteless' suggests bland food; here it means vulgar.
explanation.definitionFit: Garish means gaudy and showy, lacking good taste, so tasteless in style.

clue.text: Polish maiden enveloped by endless calm

indicators.note: endless means losing its end, so the final letter is dropped
something enveloped by another is wrapped inside it

blocks.note: to soothe is to calm
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young Polish woman is wrapped in an unending serenity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' at the start hides its lower-case sense, to buff; a maiden over is one with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: To smooth something is to polish it, making its surface even and glossy.
